t: None of the funds in this Act shall be available for the administrative expenses of making a new loan guarantee during fiscal year 1980 for any aircraft purchase loan, pursuant to the Act of September 7, 1957 (71 Stat. 629), as amended, which causes the aggregate of all such guarantees made during fiscal year 1980 to exceed $650,000,000 in principal amount: Provided, That the funds in this Act shall be available for the guarantee of loans for the refinancing of aircraft purchased after January 20, 1979, if an application for an aircraft purchase loan guarantee covering such aircraft was filed prior to that date but after October 24, 1978, and if such application meets the requirements of section 42(d) of the Airline Deregulation Act of 1978.

fable.w: This section is an appropriations limitation capping aircraft purchase loan guarantees and setting conditions for refinancing guarantees. The tempting reading is that the reference to an outside party filing an "application" amounts to participation, but applying for a loan guarantee is an application for a benefit, not consultation on a federal decision. The section provides for no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue.
fable.s: if an application for an aircraft purchase loan guarantee covering such aircraft was filed prior to that date but after October 24, 1978

opus.w: The section limits funds for aircraft purchase loan guarantees and makes some refinancing guarantees eligible based on when an application was filed. Applying for a loan guarantee is applying for a benefit, which the definition excludes from participation. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation, or right to sue.
opus.s: if an application for an aircraft purchase loan guarantee covering such aircraft was filed prior to that date but after October 24, 1978
opus.b: Someone could read this as participation because it mentions an outside party, an airline or borrower, filing an "application" for a loan guarantee. That reading doesn't hold up. The definition says applications for benefits, grants, contracts, or loans are not participation. Otherwise the section just caps how much of the appropriated funds can be spent on loan guarantees.

qwen_chat.w: This section restricts the availability of funds for loan guarantees based on aggregate amounts and specific filing dates for applications. The definition explicitly excludes 'applications for benefits, grants, contracts, or licenses' from the scope of participation. There is no requirement for the federal government to consult, coordinate with, or hold hearings for outside parties before making the decision to guarantee loans; the decision is governed by statutory caps and eligibility criteria.
qwen_chat.s: None of the funds in this Act shall be available for the administrative expenses of making a new loan guarantee during fiscal year 1980 for any aircraft purchase loan... if an application for an aircraft purchase loan guarantee covering such aircraft was filed prior to that date
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the mention of "application" implies a process where outside parties (airlines) participate in a decision. However, the definition explicitly states that "applications for benefits, grants, contracts, or licenses" are not participation. Furthermore, the text primarily restricts the use of funds based on aggregate amounts and specific dates, rather than establishing a consultation or coordination mechanism with outside parties. The "application" is merely a condition for eligibility, not a participatory process in the decision-making itself.
